newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty inches up ahead of FOMC, depos ease.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty inches up ahead of FOMC, depos ease.

text.p: The Polish zloty inched upward in very light trade ahead of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decision on whether to raise U.S. interest rates.

Dealers said turnover dwindled as players were reluctant to trade ahead of the FOMC announcement, due at about 1815 GMT, but that some currency selling pressure was felt, perhaps from banks keeping short foreign-currency positions.
"Trade was extremely thin today but some dollar-selling pressure was present late in the day," said Malgorzata Sawicka, senior dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty closed at 1.85/1.81 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than the 1.78/1.73 percent close on Monday.
It closed at 2.7890/00 to the dollar, up from 2.7930/40 on Monday and at 1.8430/40 to the mark, down from 1.8416/26.
On the money market, one-day depos inched down as the banks found excess cash after today's 592 million zloty net inflow.
Overnight rates fell to 19.4/19.7 percent from 19.6/20.1 on Monday and tomorrow/next to 19.6/19.9 percent from 19.8/20.15.
The central bank sold 372 million zlotys of 91-day and 273-day NBP-bills and average yields held flat at 19.47 and 19.90 percent. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
